plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and dense spikes of fragrant purple flowers atop slender stems. It is a favorite of bees and butterflies and is widely grown in gardens and commercial fields.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender oil was used by the ancient Romans in bathing, which is the likely origin of the plant's name from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads composed of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disk. The heads track the sun in their youth, and the plant is grown for seed, oil, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated in Ukraine, Russia, Europe, Argentina, and the United States
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is actually made up of up to 2,000 tiny individual flowers arranged in a spiral pattern following the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial prairie wildflower with drooping pink-purple petals around a prominent spiny orange-brown central cone. It is drought tolerant, attracts pollinators, and provides seeds for goldfinches in autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer into early fall (June to October)
plants.location: Native to the eastern and central United States prairies and open woodlands; grown in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The genus name comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiky central cone. Native Americans used it medicinally for centuries.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A fast-growing evergreen tree or large shrub with sickle-shaped leaves and fluffy, fragrant golden ball-shaped flower clusters. It blooms in the Southern Hemisphere's late winter, providing color during the cold season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (July to October in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1 each year.
